target_customer: AI developers and companies choosing or evaluating LLMs
problem: Teams cannot easily compare models by independent benchmark, speed and price.
business_model: Free leaderboard funnel to paid custom benchmarking, data labeling, API and evaluation tooling (ZeroEval)

founders.name: Jonathan Chavez
founders.background_notes: YC page: early employee on the LLM observability team at Datadog; first engineer at a fintech startup. Spelled Chávez on the YC page.

founders.name: Sebastian Crossa
founders.background_notes: YC page: founding engineer at Micro and Atrato. Founders met in college in Mexico; school not named.

competitors.name: LMArena
competitors.traction_then: millions of votes per a 2026 source

competitors.name: Artificial Analysis
competitors.what: Independent benchmarks plus speed and price

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating benchmarks and live API metrics is mostly data engineering; ZeroEval judges add ML work.

defensibility.rationale: Traffic and trust help, but leaderboards are replicable and rivals are established.

market_need_then: YC post reports about 60k monthly users and a third of a million unique users before the batch; demand for model comparison was high as models multiplied.

branding.name_origin: Descriptive name for LLM statistics; no origin story sourced.

identity.visual_style: Clean ranking tables and FAQ-style pages

branding.community_and_virality: Community section, Discord and X account; leaderboard traffic of about 60k MAU reported in a launch post

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name earned search traffic but is generic and sits beside the ZeroEval brand.

pivots.why: Launch post positions ZeroEval as the product; leaderboard remains the funnel.

outcome_analysis: LLM Stats built an LLM leaderboard with substantial organic traffic before YC Summer 2025 and added ZeroEval evaluation tools as the paid product. No verified funding beyond the YC deal, exit or shutdown found as of 2026-11. The traffic is a real distribution asset, while the core risk is that leaderboards are easy to copy and monetization is unproven.
notes: EveryDev, VCBacked list $500K from YC (Dealroom shows $125K); aggregators disagree, not recorded. YC page says New York; VCBacked says San Francisco. Competitor sources are 2026 so traction_then unknown. Completeness pass: a 500K round from Y Combinator in 2025 rests on a single outlet (EveryDev, also VCBacked) and is recorded as a round with stage other; Dealroom shows 125K.
